cloud_run_sizing.rationale: Founder directive 2026-07-28: size to Medium, not the script's default (min=0/max=2/mem=1Gi/cpu=1). Matches prod's own tier (deploy-worker.yml canary: --cpu 2 --memory 2Gi --min-instances 2 --max-instances 10) so latency/throughput evidence isn't an artifact of an undersized rig. min-instances=1 (vs prod's 2) chosen to avoid cold-start-induced false p99 breaches while still holding the tier down from prod's HA posture; theoretical ceiling ~800 concurrent requests (10 x 80) against the runbook's 250-peak-concurrent-session / ~83-RPS-burst target.
cloud_run_sizing.cost_note: ~$0.0822/hr Supabase Medium compute (~$60/mo) + Cloud Run pay-per-use at min-instances=1 (roughly $35-50/mo idle floor at this cpu/mem, more under 72h load) — trivial against the cost of a re-soak from undersizing.

supabase_compute_addon.connection_ceiling_resolved: Worker uses @supabase/supabase-js (PostgREST/Supavisor pooler), not raw pg.Pool -- confirmed via grep, no direct connection pool in services/worker/src. Effective ceiling for the hot request path is connections_pooler=600, not connections_direct=120. Cloud Run ceiling (10 max-instances x 80 concurrency = 800 theoretical concurrent requests) exceeds the 600 pooler ceiling in the extreme case, but the runbook's A5 target (250 peak concurrent sessions) and A4 RPS figures (28 sustained / 83 burst) sit comfortably under 600. This closes the runbook's SS0.6 bottleneck #3 (previously 'must be pulled live, listed as a named open verification') with a real number: max_connections=120 direct / 600 pooler at Medium, vs an un-exceeded product of realistic concurrent load.

anti_hollow_verification.getblock_rpc_finding: ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-28 (go/no-go blocker #1). Two candidate GetBlock-labeled secrets exist and BOTH are dead ends, not a simple wiring fix: (1) the rig's actual BITCOIN_RPC_URL secret (arkova-s33-rig-b1-bitcoin-core-signet-rpc-url) resolves to http://10.33.10.10:38332 -- a PRIVATE-IP self-hosted Bitcoin Core node from an unrelated prior rig (S3.3 rig-b1), reachable only via VPC connector `arkova-s33-b1-signet-vpc` (confirmed READY via `gcloud compute networks vpc-access connectors list`), which is NOT attached to this soak's Cloud Run service (no vpc-access annotation on arkova-worker-launch-72h-2026-08-staging) -- explains the Node `fetch failed` (no route to a private RFC1918 host from this service's network). This is not actually GetBlock at all, just mislabeled as an 'override' during provisioning. (2) The literal `GetBlock` secret in Secret Manager (https://go.getblock.io/<token>, same URL shape as prod's working bitcoin-rpc-url) was tested directly via curl against the live GetBlock endpoint and returned HTTP 200 body {"error":"Unknown token"} -- the credential itself is invalid/expired/wrong-plan, independent of network reachability. Prod's own bitcoin-rpc-url secret (https://go.getblock.io/<different-token>) was NOT tested against (never touch prod's mainnet-scoped token from a rig context) but is architecturally the same shape, confirming GetBlock's hosted-endpoint pattern is right -- this rig simply has no valid signet-scoped token provisioned. CONCLUSION: GetBlock genuinely cannot be made to work on signet with currently available credentials in this session (no valid signet GetBlock token exists in Secret Manager; the only non-mempool alternative is a differently-scoped private node with no network path to this rig). Per the runbook's own pre-approved fallback wording (docs/lane1/s33-multiorg-harness-design.md line 70), proceeding on the disclosed exception below rather than blocking the soak indefinitely.

anti_hollow_verification.feature_flags_boot_order_bug_found: flagRegistry.init() runs ONCE at worker boot with no refresh/poll loop. The initial deploy (00001-x6k) cached switchboard_flags BEFORE this session mirrored prod's flags onto the rig, so ENABLE_BATCH_ANCHORING read false at boot (00001) despite the DB row already being true by the time of the first forced-run test. Required a service restart (00002) to pick up the mirrored DB flags. Any future rig standup must mirror switchboard_flags and set env-only flags BEFORE the first Cloud Run deploy, or must force a restart after -- this is a repeatable trap, not a one-off.
anti_hollow_verification.org_credit_enforcement_env_only_bug_foun: ENABLE_ORG_CREDIT_ENFORCEMENT is hardcoded env-source-only in services/worker/src/middleware/flagRegistry.ts:30 (`() => config.enableOrgCreditEnforcement`), unlike every other switchboard-mirrored flag. Mirroring it into switchboard_flags as true had ZERO effect on worker behavior until an explicit Cloud Run --update-env-vars=ENABLE_ORG_CREDIT_ENFORCEMENT=true was applied (revision 00003-dw8). A soak relying on the DB mirror alone for this flag would have silently run with credit enforcement OFF -- exactly the R17-divergence-silently-reverts hollow-soak risk the pre-mortem SS1 named, but via a different mechanism (env-only flag wiring, not a skipped mirror step).
